claim.summary: In a binary Boolean degree-D pseudoideal, fixed A degree<=a,U<=P_K, r fixed inputs degree<=delta>=1 and h>=1 rows, assume a+K+(h+2)delta<=D. For input span B and realized j-row prefix P_j set W_j=image f->(A P_j g_i f) on B^(h-j)U, d_j=dimW_j. Conditional fresh uniform row gives E[d_(j+1)|history]<=d_j/2. If h<=r and coefficient rows are sampled uniformly outside their prior span, the factor is (2^(r-j-1)-1)/(2^(r-j)-1). Thus 2^(-(h-j))d_j is a supermartingale for the first law, and terminal bounds equal existing input-word/independent-row bounds. Subtraction for old-span rows applies to the containing row-kernel intersection, not automatically W_(j+1). Full feature-function saturation has d_j=2^(r-rank C_j)-1, also for the recorded two-layer disjoint-conjunction realization; adaptive selection gives no better universal independent-row factor.
claim.assessment: Working explicit conditional composition of existing arbitrary-domain shortening and input-word estimates. Medium reviewed. Complete algebraic all-parameter saturation and source ledger retained; no new numerical tests or hard-family obstruction.

Binary input-word prefix certificates inherit this factor at their original buffer and full replay cost.

claim.summary: Predictable invertible affine recentering of uniform coefficient rows preserves their joint law and every actual error-rank statistic. Over F2 in a Boolean degree-D pseudoideal, M degree-delta tuples admitting literal decompositions into degree-d references plus at most r high directions in their original constant spans have common weighted removal with r_a+t legal rows, if b+K+(r+1)delta+t*d<=D and M(1-eta)^t<1, eta=N_n(K-d)/(2N_n(K)). The common surviving weight is wf, deg f<=K; no prefix-weight survival is assumed.
